title: With Joy We Hail the Sacred Day
description: With Joy We Hail the Sacred Day in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Harriet Auber wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 128.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: With joy we hail the sa-cred day Which we have called God’s own; With joy the sum-mons we o-bey To wor-ship at His throne.

lines: With joy we hail the sacred day
Which we have called God’s own;
With joy the summons we obey
To worship at His throne.
Thy chosen temple, Lord, how fair!
As here Thy servants throng
To breathe the humble, fervent prayer
And pour the choral song.
Spirit of Grace, O deign to dwell
Within Thy Church below;
Make her in holiness excel,
With pure devotion glow.
Let peace within her walls be found;
Let all her sons unite
To spread with holy zeal around
Her clear and shining light.
Great God, we hail the sacred day
Which we have called Thine own;
With joy the summons we obey
To worship at Thy throne.

licence: Public domain: Harriet Auber died in 1862.
credits: Words by Harriet Auber (1773–1862), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
